Hi, this is my first comment on your site. I love that this site shows the upvotes and downvotes because it allows me to gauge how many people found the comment significant enough to vote on it, and not just the ratio. It's also comforting, for example, when you get downvoted a lot, that if you can see a few upvotes it tells you that at least some people agreed with you. It's also more open and less cryptic. And you allow more privacy and account deletion. I also think Reddit is becoming too insular.

Anyway, I have a few possible ideas on how to improve voting:

-Only allow votes on the submission if users go to the comments. This creates an extra barrier that will prevent careless and lazy voters - especially ones who don't even click the article but merely vote on the title alone. Don't even have vote buttons on the front page but instead merely show the up and down scores. Maybe you could even require someone to click on the article link before being able to vote on the submission. This might irritate some users, but overall I bet it would improve the quality substantially.

-Only allow votes on a comment if a "vote reply" is made to the comment. When users click the vote arrow, they would be prompted with a field asking them to comment why they are voting. This forces users to actually consider why they found the comment non-constructive and to supply a counter-argument. It would also create a barrier to lazy voters and voters who vote on impulse and without really considering why they are downvoting. Even forcing users to write a reply that "I downvoted you because I disagree" could force a lot more accountability and integrity. To reduce clutter, these "vote reply" comments would be differentiated in the UI and minimized and nested below the comment being voted on to differentiate them from normal replies. Normal replies could still be made to comments without voting if the user simply wants to discuss the topic at hand. Finally, a "vote reply" could be toggled with a checkbox to leave it un-minimized so that it could be more visible as a proper reply, if that's the user's preference.

These ideas might seem shocking and unappealing to users used to Reddit, but I think they would go a long way towards improving the quality and meaningfulness of votes. I know these ideas are not fully formed so I'm hoping maybe they'll even inspire some other even better ideas from others. If these are terrible ideas, I'm sorry for filling your brain with nonsense.

I've seen a similar suggestion to this a while ago and I have the same view on it as before.

  • Adding a barrier to the voting system will only decrease participation, rather than increase the ratio of proper voting to improper voting.

    Though what we're talking about is purely theoretical, there is no evidence that this will work. The problem I see here is that the solution you proposed isn't the best solution to this problem because it will likely give people like me a headache. Example:

    I see a submission about a funny kitten. I click the link in a new tab and laugh at the picture. I close the tab and go back to WhoaVerse to vote on the submission. Now, what would've been a quick upvote and move on, I now have to click on 'comments', loading a completely new page, to actually vote on it.

    Going through many submissions in this way would just decrease the odds of me voting on them. The best user interface always focuses on as few steps in each task as possible.

  • Adding a 'vote reply' restriction would decrease participation at worst and increase spam at best.

    I've made this argument before. Firstly, in order to avoid misunderstanding, I'm going to define what I think proper voting is in order to understand why I think this option is unnecessary. I believe that comment voting should be about relevancy and never opinion. No one should ever upvote or downvote a comment based on whether or not they agreed or not, but whether or not the comment belonged there.

    With this in mind, it is pointless to add an option like this because this type of view on comment voting only allows few reasons to vote: how relevant a comment is. If I disagree with someone, I upvote their comment — since it's relevant to the discussion most of the time — and state a reply of disagreement. If I downvote a comment, it is almost always because it was either irrelevant or spam, never anything else. If the downvote needed clarification, I would provide it, but, generally, it's pretty straightforward.

    No user should be forced to comment.
